question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function
question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{3+4x}{2-3x}$ and the point $P(1,-7)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(-7,1).$
question.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(1,-7).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3+4x}{2-3x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{17}{(2-3x)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =17\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(1,-7)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(-7,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(-7) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-7))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{17}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
